hook_text: In 1834 six farm workers were shipped to the other side of the world. Their crime? An oath.
clip_script: Dorset, 1834. Farm workers earn seven shillings a week and the bosses want to cut it again. So six men do something brave: they form a union, and they swear an oath to stick together. The authorities dig up an old law against secret oaths. The sentence: seven years' transportation to Australia. But Britain is furious. Tens of thousands march through London. Around eight hundred thousand people sign a petition. In 1836, the six are pardoned. They become heroes. Their story sits in a long fight: Luddites smashing machines, a peaceful crowd attacked at Peterloo, Chartists demanding the vote, matchgirls and dockers winning strikes. And it reaches all the way to South Africa, where today the Constitution protects every worker's right to join a union and to strike.
visual_style: A whiteboard village with six stick figures in a circle, a gavel falling, a ship sailing to Australia, then a petition scroll unrolling across the screen and the ship sailing back.
pacing: Quiet start, rising anger at the sentence, triumphant beat at the pardon, quick montage to the present.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and see how workers won the right to organise.
